text:
alice (Support): Customer BrightWave (acct brightwave-eu) on Dedicated EU2 reporting repeated 429s and p99 tail latency spikes over the past 48h. They see errors during sustained traffic bursts to gpt-opus-13b. Can SRE confirm noisy-neighbor on pool eu2-dedicated-3?

mike (SRE): looking at infra telemetry now. host node-44 shows SM util bursts up to 98% around 02:14UTC, GPU memory util stays ~60% -> SM saturation pattern. KV cache miss rate jumped right before the spikes.

joanna (ML Eng): what are their request shapes? small batches or large? KV churn can cause tail blowups.

alice (Support): they sent example: many concurrent small requests ~= 350-450 rps, batch_size=1, seq_len~1024, no prefix caching enabled. customer says retries spike billing.

mike (SRE): confirmed concurrency ~420, p95->p99 increased from 180ms to 1.8s during bursts. autoscaler tried to spin a new node but pool reached reserved capacity. infra-bot shows "no spare capacity in eu2".

infra-bot: [autoscale] attempted provisioning 1 node for pool eu2-dedicated-3 at 02:16UTC, status=FAILED, reason=quota/reserved-capacity-exhausted.

mike (SRE): likely noisy neighbor due to mixed MIG packing on some hosts: node-44 has mixed slices (1g_10gb + 2g_20gb) which causes variable SM/pcie contention under these small-batch high-concurrency workloads. can we get a quick nvml snapshot from the host?

joanna (ML Eng): repro plan I suggest: reproduce load in staging with identical MIG config and request shape. quick commands:

```
# on node
nvidia-smi dmon -s u -o DT
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,clocks.gr --format=csv -l 1
# run client load (example)
w rk -t8 -c420 -d120s --latency http://staging-eu2/proxy/load
```
joanna (ML Eng): also capture inference logs with kvcache diagnostics enabled and trace ids so we can correlate spikes to KV eviction churn.

mike (SRE): short mitigation options: 1) temporarily move BrightWave to an isolated host (eu2-dedicated-isolated-1) with single-tenant packing, 2) apply a per-tenant concurrency cap / rate limit on the route to smooth bursts, 3) if we can't isolate, repack pool to homogeneous MIG slices.

alice (Support): customer is sensitive to downtime but willing to try a short traffic switch. I'll propose the isolated host option and ask if we can schedule a 30m migration window. Also they'll need a credit for retry charges.

mike (SRE): I can trigger a manual migration to eu2-dedicated-isolated-1 and pin their model instance. Will need approval from infra on capacity. Tagging @oncall-sre.

joanna (ML Eng): I'll spin the staging repro with mixed-MIG packing and the exact request traces from BrightWave. Creating internal ticket INF-7891 to track analysis + repro artifacts. I'll attach nvidia-smi dumps, KV cache metrics, and request traces.

alice (Support): filing support ticket to customer: proposed actions (1) short migration to isolated host, (2) enable client-side exponential backoff to avoid billing spikes, (3) we will follow up with root-cause from INF-7891.

mike (SRE): quick helper snippet to collect NVML and MIG layout for host-44:

```
nvidia-smi -q -d MIG | sed -n '1,200p' > /tmp/host44_mig.txt
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,memory.total,memory.free,utilization.gpu,utilization.memory --format=csv -l 2 > /tmp/gpu_dumps.csv &
```

mike (SRE): once we have dumps I'll look for SM util imbalance and PCIe stalls. If confirmed, we should avoid mixed packing for this workload.

alice (Support): thanks all — I'll update BrightWave with the migration window proposal and CC INF-7891. please update this thread when the migration is scheduled. @mike @joanna @infra-bot :thumbsup:
